facts.text: Case3 calls SetTimer(window,100,10000,NULL), stores its returned value atUI+12b8 and setsUI+1186=0 before connection. Original return success and actual timer delivery were not observed.
Observed WM_TIMER map row points to414a00. Timer100 calls KillTimer with stored value, removes wait item, marksUI+1186=1, closes channel and restores UI; it does not rotate endpoints in this branch.

Catch-like block checks current endpoint versus wrapped previous(first-1), andUI+1186. Continuing path advances(current+1)%count, copies address/port, sets local retry flag1 and closes the channel. Continuation tests that flag and jumps41171b. The native additional cleanup comparison is unwrapped first-1; independent controller does not copy that edge case or treat pseudocode self-call as recursion.

Initial index uses native random/scaling and divisor32767.0; first index and previous wrapped index are separate stack values. New core requires a caller-supplied valid ordinal instead of copying this RNG/scaling behavior.

Writable wait repeats capacity query,context service andSleep1 with no local time bound/cancel predicate. The context wrapper calls service helpers; complete downstream Windows message scheduling was not established. New async controller performs no busy-wait or sleep.

Success/failure reset paths call the timer-cancellation helper, mark UI completion and close channel; success increments wizard stage. Connection close callback sends local result-100 only while its separate C+0c flag is false. Close removes manager mapping and clears two connection token words; current callback and UI flags are not authentication proof.
Wizard stage>=5 can call game launch and then reset stage3. Independent flow produces only unverified selection data and does not execute game/update/registration actions.

independent_policy.scope: Post-local-preconditions single login exchange; pure bytes/local control state only
independent_policy.endpoint_count: 1..10, explicit first ordinal; circular one pass only on opening failure before opened event
independent_policy.replay: No automatic retry after opened/credential submission; new flow required for a new user attempt
independent_policy.clock: Explicit nondecreasing safe integer milliseconds; one10000ms deadline from start; boundary wins before packet/open processing; no deadline reset on failover
independent_policy.attempt_id: Local routing identity only, never a wire field; noncurrent events ignored before touching clock or buffers
independent_policy.challenge: Incremental exact supported challenge; bounded2122B, strict ASCII hex, no trailing pre-answer ciphertext; caller explicitly supplies20 exponent bytes
independent_policy.final_reply: Type2 preliminary notices<=64; type11 final must be last complete message in the batch with no pending record/frame; close intent emitted. Later events ignored.
independent_policy.ownership: Outputs are owned byte copies; internal choices cannot be changed via returned models; cancel/select/failure release internal buffers and schedules best effort, not guaranteed JS erasure
not_native_equivalence: Strict monotonic hard deadline versus Windows queued WM_TIMER delivery

Strict final batch/count/group/shape policies and no native UI/process side effects
